Do you have a crock pot? If so, get yourself a whole chicken, some baking potatoes, and a bag of frozen veg. Unwrap your whole chicken and remove neck/gizzards (put them in the fridge for later.) Put the whole chicken into the crock pot. Set crock pot on high and let cook 6-7 hours (do this when you first wake up.) By the time dinner rolls round, pop those taters in the oven and bake them. Put those veggies in a pot about 15 minutes before you're ready to eat. That chicken will pull right off the bone and you've got yourself a filling and healthy meal. Later (the next morning) when the chicken is completely cool, pull the rest of the meat (all of it!) off the chicken and set it aside. Put the chicken skin, bones, neck, and gizzards back into the crock pot. Pour some fresh water over the chicken bones (until they are just about covered.) Add a Tablespoon of salt, an onion (peeled and cut in half,) a few carrots, some celery stalks, and cook on low for about 6-7 hours. Once it's cool, pour the broth through a fine strainer into a container (I use mason jars.) Now you have your own super healthy bone broth. You can use this and the chicken meat to make soups, chicken pot pies, chicken tetrazzini, what have you. You can also make delicious chicken sandwiches, cranberry chicken salad, or throw that chicken meat over some greens and call it lunch.

Hope this helps. :)

Right, so last night I sat down to post a recipe to v/cooking when it occured to me that I don't use proper measurements. I mostly "measure" by sight and taste. I'll have to start measuring my ingredients as I go so I can type up my recipes. (Also, Voat was down, so I wasn't able to post regardless.) I'll just leave this quick chicken noodle soup recipe here until I can come up with some proper instructions (sorry!):

After you've cooked your whole chicken/removed all the meat/made your bone broth/cleaned your crock pot: dump a litre jar of bone broth into your pot. Refill the jar with fresh water and pour this into the pot as well. Wash/peel/chop a few carrots (I use about 6 large,) wash/chop a few celery stalks (also about 6,) and dice one whole onion. Put your veg into a pan with a knob of butter over medium heat. Cook the veg about 5 minutes, give it a stir here and there. Put the veg in the pot and add the ckicken meat. (I use about half what I've pulled off the chicken.) Add a dash of salt and pepper, a dash of turmeric, a dash of oregano, and a few basil leaves. (Play with the seasonings as your tastes may be different.) Set your crock pot to low for about 6-7 hours. About 15 minutes before you're ready to eat add the egg noodles. (Again, I do this by sight and it ends up being about half the bag.) We usually eat our soups with a nice chunk of warm crusty bread.
